title: Why Nvidia Stock Took a Dive Today
detail:
Why Nvidia Stock Took a Dive Today
Danny Vena, CPA, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 3:49 PM EDT 3 min read
NVDA
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) was part of a broad sell-off in the tech sector on Friday, with shares falling as much as 5.3%. As of 2:11 p.m. ET, the stock was still down 5.2%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

While the tech downdraft was certainly a contributor, the catalyst that sent the chipmaker lower was the rising cost of artificial intelligence (AI) and the question of who will pay for it all.

Image source: Nvidia.

You have to spend money to make money

Reports emerged today that Nvidia may be considering another financing deal with a customer. The company is reportedly in talks to provide billions of dollars in credit guarantees for an Nscale data center that will ultimately be used by Anthropic, according to Bloomberg, which cited "a person familiar with the matter."

This marks the latest in a growing string of financing and credit commitments Nvidia has made. For example, reports from earlier this week suggest the company has data center-related commitments and guarantees of $165 billion, according to a report that first appeared in The Information.

That's not all. Nvidia also holds more than $63 billion in equity stakes in publicly traded companies, according to a recent regulatory filing. Many of those stakes are in the chipmaker's customers, either directly or indirectly. When you include start-ups, that figure climbs to $99 billion.

This has fueled fears among some investors of the repercussions if AI adoption slows or someone builds a better mousetrap than Nvidia's industry-leading graphics processing units (GPUs). If that were to happen, it could be the catalyst that starts the dominoes falling, and the AI trade could all unravel -- or so the popular narrative goes.

Yet a look at Nvidia's recent financials should help put those fears to rest. For the company's fiscal 2027 second quarter (ended July 26), the chipmaker generated revenue of $96 billion, up 106% year over year -- and expects that figure to rise to $108 billion when it reports its Q3 results in mid-November.

Moreover, Nvidia carries more than $99 billion in cash and marketable securities on its balance sheet, which, in my opinion, provides sufficient liquidity to cover its various financing and credit commitments. We'll have more details when Nvidia releases its next earnings report after the market close on Nov. 17.

title: Forget Rescheduling: Green Thumb's Cash Flow Is the Real Reason to Own It

Forget Rescheduling: Green Thumb's Cash Flow Is the Real Reason to Own It
Thomas Niel, The Motley Fool

For marijuana stocks, regulatory clarity remains a key issue. Progress such as federal rescheduling remains stymied. However, for Green Thumb (OTC: GTBIF), a multi-state operator (MSO), or operator of cannabis businesses licensed at the U.S. state level, federal regulatory clarity isn't a necessary ingredient for profitability. This is especially true considering the company's relatively high cash flow.

If regulatory progress gains momentum, Green Thumb's stock price could rise more rapidly than the prices of better-known yet unprofitable names like Aurora Cannabis or Canopy Growth.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
Green Thumb is "in the green" in more ways than one

Green Thumb doesn't only have a "green thumb" in terms of the size of its cannabis cultivation, marketing, and sales operation. Unlike its competitors, which are still unprofitable, Green Thumb has been consistently profitable, with strong operating cash flow to boot. For instance, in 2025, the company reported GAAP earnings of $114.2 million, operating cash flow of $294.9 million, and normalized EBITDA of $348.4 million, or a nearly 30% EBITDA margin.

EBITDA and cash flow are very high relative to Green Thumb's $1.4 billion market cap and $1.7 billion enterprise value. Moreover, the company continues to put its cash flow to good use, devoting much of it to share repurchases. Under its current share repurchase program, Green Thumb has repurchased approximately $203.4 million in stock and remains authorized to repurchase an additional $62.3 million.

As for more recent results? Normalized EBITDA has remained at $84.3 million in second-quarter 2026. Although operating cash flow during the first half of 2026 fell to $104.8 million from $130.7 million in the prior year's quarter, factors such as Green Thumb's further expansion in the United States, including new locations in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, may help explain this drop.

Regulatory progress remains a top catalyst

Existing profitability may be the key reason to buy Green Thumb over its more well-known peers, but don't expect high earnings and a low valuation to serve as their own catalyst. As 280E regulations, which affect the deductibility of most cannabis business operations, remain in place, and the U.S. federal government's overall position on marijuana remains unclear, even profitable cannabis companies will keep trading at low multiples to EBITDA and operating cash flow.

Rich Smith, The Motley Fool

Firefly Aerospace (NASDAQ:FLY), the first space stock to land a spacecraft on the moon with 100% success, tumbled 11.1% through 2:40 p.m. Friday.

That's the bad news. The good news is that there doesn't seem to be any particular reason for Firefly to be going down.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Firefly Aerospace.

What's wrong with Firefly stock today?

We're right in the middle of earnings season for aerospace stocks, with Lockheed Martin beating earnings last week and Boeing an earnings miss just earlier this week. Firefly, on the other hand, hasn't reported any earnings at all and isn't scheduled to do so until Nov. 10. There hasn't been any recent news of analyst downgrades or changes to the stock's price target either.

In the absence of any such catalyst, there's really no reason for Firefly stock to be crashing.

On the contrary, what news there is on Firefly is of the "good news" variety. Last week, Firefly passed preliminary design work on its MoonFall mission for NASA -- a $75 million contract to deploy "hopping" space drones to the moon -- and is on course to hit its late 2028 launch date. On Wednesday, Firefly confirmed that its SciTec subsidiary passed a milestone test on its even bigger $259 million FORGE software contract for the U.S. Space Force.

What's next for Firefly stock

So if Firefly's got nothing but good news to report, why is the stock falling? I suppose this could be a case of investors bracing for bad news in the upcoming earnings report, but honestly, Wall Street has set a pretty low bar there.

Last year, Firefly lost $0.55 per share in its Q3; this time, all analysts want to see is for that loss to shrink 9%. So long as Firefly loses no more than $0.50 per share, Wall Street should be happy.

As fast as Firefly stock fell today, I wouldn't be a bit surprised to see the stock bounce back even quicker.

title: Tech stocks crushed as Nasdaq tumbles nearly 1,000 points
detail:
Tech stocks crushed as Nasdaq tumbles nearly 1,000 points
Mary Cunningham
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 3:09 PM EDT 3 min read
GOOG
NVDA
^IXIC
INTC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The Nasdaq Composite Index tumbled more than 970 points, or 3.7%, in afternoon trading, while other U.S. financial markets also swooned as investors pulled back amid growing concerns about the health of the critical technology sector.

Intel's stock plunged more than 30%, while shares of Google's parent, Alphabet, continued to wobble after the company's Class A stock slid more than 12% on Thursday, its worst day since the company went public as Google in 2004. The drop erased roughly $500 billion in Alphabet's market value.

Shares of Nvidia, the maker of advanced chips used to power AI models and a bellwether for the sector, also dropped 5%.

"This has been one of the worst tech earnings seasons in memory, with underwhelming results from a slew of very prominent companies," market analyst Adam Crisafulli, head of Vital Knowledge, said in a research note.

"The slump in tech stocks (and the attendant deterioration in tech sentiment) isn't simply a financial phenomenon and could undermine industry fundamentals by making it more difficult for companies to raise incremental debt and equity," he added in a separate report.

The negative sentiment around tech spread to other major stock indices on Friday. The S&P 500 shed 183 points, or 2.4%, while the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average sank 746 points, or 1.4%.

Debt reckoning?

The weaker-than-expected tech earnings reports are heightening concerns that massive investments in AI will not generate the payoff Wall Street expects. Investors are also worried about the debt companies are taking on to finance data center capital expenditures and whether that debt is sustainable.

"Mega-cap stocks have faced increased selling pressure over the past two weeks as elevated AI-related spending and rising financing costs raise concerns over the path to profitability," Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist for brokerage firm LPL Financial, said in an email. "Recent earnings reports have added to these concerns, revealing slowing growth in select hyperscalers' core businesses."

Another factor weighing on tech stocks is investor expectations that the Federal Reserve will have to keep raising interest rates to curb economic growth and subdue inflation, which remains elevated.

The central bank left its benchmark rate unchanged this week, but many economists think it will hike rates as early as December and into 2027. That would make it more expensive for companies to borrow money to build the data centers required to power AI services, cutting into corporate profits.

AMZN Stock Set To Drop For Third Straight Week: Amazon Taps $80B Credit Line To Fund AI Capex
Shashank Nayar
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 3:37 PM EDT 3 min read
AMZN
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Amazon secured access to up to $80 billion in discretionary borrowing through supplier financing agreements running from early 2027 through Q3 2028.

Heavy investments in data centers and equipment led to a $42.4 billion free cash outflow for the year ended Sept. 30.

Leaving behind its traditional cash-and-bonds approach, Amazon is embracing flexible collateralized financing alongside competitors to purchase costly hardware like Nvidia AI chips.

Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) has arranged up to $80 billion in supplier financing credit line as it prepares for aggressive infrastructure spending to power its artificial intelligence initiatives.

The new credit structure gives the e-commerce and cloud provider additional financial flexibility while committing hundreds of billions toward data center construction and advanced hardware.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

AMZN stock eased about 2% on Friday and is set to end its third consecutive week lower.

New Way Of Funding

According to a quarterly regulatory filing disclosed Thursday, the secured credit line allows Amazon to borrow against the value of purchased hardware at its own discretion.

The facility opens at the start of 2027 and runs through the third quarter of 2028. Lenders participating in the agreement will hold collateral rights over specific assets acquired via the facility. Amazon has not detailed which specific equipment will serve as collateral, and representatives for the company declined to provide further specifics.

Speaking on Bloomberg Television on Friday, Matt Garman, Chief Executive Officer of Amazon Web Services, highlighted the rationale behind the strategy. "When we see such a really large opportunity in front of us, we're looking for ways to also responsibly fund that so that we can go as big as possible for our customers," Garman said. He added that the firm is collaborating with key partners to better balance operational cash flows during this rapid operational buildup.

Shift From Traditional Funding

Historically, Amazon financed its cloud computing infrastructure and semiconductor acquisitions directly from retail and cloud revenue streams or through corporate bond issuances.

The company previously refrained from complex financing arrangements, such as joint venture construction deals or third-party chip leases. Such structures have become commonplace among competing technology companies seeking to acquire expensive Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) processors, which represent a significant portion of modern data center expenditures.

title: Nvidia’s GPU Rents Surge as Anthropic’s Revenue Has “Gone Vertical,” Says Gavin Baker
detail:
Nvidia’s GPU Rents Surge as Anthropic’s Revenue Has “Gone Vertical,” Says Gavin Baker
Roxanna Maglangit
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:14 PM EDT 5 min read
NVDA
ANTH.PVT
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Nvidia's GPU Rents Surge as Anthropic's Revenue Has "Gone Vertical," Says Gavin Baker ©SteveLuker from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Anthropic's S-1, filed Monday, shows $2.08 of revenue per dollar of compute, up from $0.40 a year earlier, according to an analysis Gavin Baker endorsed.

Baker argues that cheaper tokens raise total spending on compute, which supports demand and pricing for NVIDIA's GPUs.

Analysts expect NVIDIA's revenue to grow from $215.9 billion in fiscal 2026 to $692 billion in fiscal 2028, but rising memory costs are expected to cut gross margin to 71% to 72% in the January 2027 quarter.

NVIDIA trades at 18x forward earnings, compared with a three-year average of 30x, ahead of its Nov. 17 report.

Anthropic's S-1 came out Monday. It gave NVIDIA (NVDA:NASDAQ) bulls the number they'd been waiting for.

Gavin Baker, who runs Atreides Management, had said the filing would "break a lot of people's brains," because so many macro and value investors assume "tokens are subsidized." On Tuesday, he posted: "Brains were indeed broken."

The day before, he'd made the case on X:

"I am shocked, absolutely shocked, that Anthropic ARR has likely gone vertical in October after they cut token prices. Except the exact same thing happened for the entire AI market, which is why GPU rental prices have surged while token prices declined."

That's a big claim. It's also the whole bull case for NVIDIA in two sentences.

TIKR tracks 62 analysts on Nvidia. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Nvidia, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Nvidia's Analyst Ratings

The filing backs him up

The October number is Baker's own estimate, since the S-1's figures stop at June 30. But what the filing does show points the same way.

An X account, @AGTPinsights, pointed out that the filing shows "$2.08 of revenue per compute dollar now versus $0.40 a year ago, even with lower prices." Baker answered with one word: "Indeed."

So each dollar Anthropic spends on compute now brings in about five times as much revenue as it did a year ago, even though prices are lower. And the company is profitable: GAAP operating income was $974 million in the second quarter, an 8% operating margin.

Baker says every data point on AI so far has shown this kind of elasticity: lower prices lead to so much more use that total spending goes up. He also argues that revenue per GPU can rise as token prices fall, as long as each GPU produces enough extra tokens. If what Anthropic pays for GPUs rises by less than that combined effect, both its revenue and its margins can grow.
